chunks: Sulayman ibn 'Isa narrated from his father, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How should I perform your Ziyarah if I am not able to come?' He said to me, 'O 'Isa! When you are not able to come, if it is Friday, perform Ghusl or Wudu, ascend to your roof, pray two Rak'ah, and turn toward me. Verily, whoever visits me during my life has visited me after my death, and whoever visits me after my death has visited me during my life.'
ai.seo_question: How to perform remote Ziyarah to the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) outlines the ritual of 'Ziyarat al-Ghā'ib' (visitation of the absent), emphasizing that spiritual presence transcends physical distance through purification, prayer, and directional orientation (qibla of the heart). This tradition underscores the Shia belief in the continuity of the Imam's spiritual authority and accessibility, affirming that the merit of visiting the Imam remains constant whether he is alive or in the grave, thereby validating remote devotion as a complete act of worship.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. Sulaymān ibn ‘Isā narrated from his father, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “How should I perform your Ziyārah if I am not able to (come to visit you?)” Imam (a.s.) replied: O ‘Isā! When you are not able to come (to my Ziyārah), perform a Ghusl or Wuďū on a Friday, ascend to the roof of your house, establish two Rak’ah of prayers, and then turn toward the direction of my location. Verily those who come to visit me during my life (are like those who) have performed my Ziyārah after my death, and those who perform my Ziyārah after my death (are like those who) have come to visit me during my life.
